name: Sanctions Compliance Review
description: Raised by flow 2 (quote-bind) when a sanctions screen returns a hit at bind time. Investigate the hit against policy_config.sanctions_state and resolve it — clear the policy to bind, or escalate. This task does not carry the `referral` tag, so flow 11 ignores any status move made on it (the tag gate, not the status, is what stops a compliance review from accidentally issuing a quote).

task_actions.description: Record the sanctions screening outcome and resolution

_notes.priority_and_tag: Both copied verbatim from contract artefact 4: priority `highest` (spec §4.4.3 'urgent') and tag `sanctions`, both written by flow 2 on this task kind.
_notes.no_referral_tag: This is the load-bearing exclusion, not an omission. Flow 11's gate 2 requires `referral` IN task.tags; a Sanctions Compliance Review task carries `sanctions` only, so moving it to Approved never issues a quote — even though `approved` is a shared status id across all four templates in this one space (artefact 4's vocabulary is shared by design, per A4-4).
_notes.form_action: Pinned to policy_config (which carries `sanctions_state`) with no named view, same reasoning as the Underwriting Review template — policy_config has only a `table` view today, verified by reading record_configs/policy_config.json (not edited).
_notes.assignees: Deliberately left unset — see the Underwriting Review template's note; no real compliance-user id exists on this staging account to hardcode.
